tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
We can reflect an object in any line. Consider the diagram below. The two polygons are the mirror images of each other in the line $l.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222660/assets/1e4dfb2939916df5d5018320819f14fcec261a1e77c171b551e9868a8c3bebc8.png)

If we want to reflect the quadrilateral $ABCD$ below in the line $l,$ we can reflect each vertex separately and then draw the segments between the resulting corresponding vertices.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222660/assets/a47c41b41ecae2bc4c281e1b90c843ae68fa907a0d2ff49c48454fd80e2977c7.png)

Let's start by reflecting the point $A.$ To do this, we need to plot a new point $A'$ on the opposite side of $l$ at an equal distance away from $l$ as the original point $A.$

The original point $A$ is $4$ units to the left of $l,$ so we need to plot the new point $A'$ at a distance of $4$ units to the right of $l.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222660/assets/33bb82c9d0f20df13f46060b9aec21e8c4d1231766926c47b7718bf58e1c5e32.png)

Now let's reflect other vertices of the quadrilateral in the same way:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222660/assets/00ec763ccce462effa024486a6ff09a98b549c61179de18bb850470e835a7627.png)

Finally, we draw segments between the reflected vertices.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222660/assets/7ffd0cfa45051d8376c46528370b34222a1ebb226987e7530d5081d69942bbde.png)

tutorials.name: Identifying the Line of Reflection
tutorials.problem:
If we're given two points, we can find the line of reflection that maps one point onto another by finding the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the two points.

For example, suppose that the line $l$ reflects the point $A$ onto $A'$ below. How can we find the equation of $l?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222660/assets/79ddc15badc704a9c9860207a5156c3a0505ab626572581bcf3146976338a015.png)

The line $l$ is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment $\overline{AA'}.$ So, the line of reflection is $y=-1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222660/assets/aa240e562acf388bdf05751e680e917bc8465bad34300334f6b423df46a7d1f3.png)
